analysis.title: Industrial Metals Weekly: Base metals equities under pressure despite supply tightness
key_insights: Copper equities fell 1.5% w/w while copper was relatively flat. The tech selloff on doubts over AI spending put the AI-demand narrative behind copper's rally under renewed scrutiny.
The Intel and Amazon selloffs hit AI-linked names, and the Fed hold with two dissents in favour of a hike added pressure to equities.
Views from LME week were mixed on future AI-driven demand, citing a stark disconnect between AI capex and actual metals demand.
Physical conditions remain tight: the Yangshan premium is near $200/t (363% YoY) and Chinese copper inventories are drawn down to 44kt (down 57% YoY).

Cochilco now expects Chilean copper output to fall 8.4% in 2026 versus a prior estimate of a 2.6% decline, and a 3% recovery in 2027, lower than previously expected. It cites lower ore grades, maintenance and disruptions.
RBC fine-tuned its FCX cost estimates to match company guidance. FCX 2026E adjusted EPS is $3.54, with the prior estimate at $4.33.

Chart of the Week: older copper mines face falling head grades, deeper pits, longer haul distances and rising sustaining capex. New discoveries have collapsed and projects can take over a decade to reach production. RBC reads the age profile as support for the structural supply case and a higher incentive price.
Base metals were mixed on the week: copper -0.3% to $6.55/lb, nickel -1.9% to $6.91/lb, zinc +1.5% to $1.79/lb. Met coal fell 0.9% to $264.4/mt and iron ore rose 0.4% to $91.10/dmt.
North American copper producers trade at 0.8x P/NAV against a 10-year average of 0.9x and a 3-year average of 1.0x. Global diversifieds trade at 1.0x against a 10-year average of 0.9x.
FCX trades at 0.82x P/NAV at spot (1.13x at RBC deck prices). Its weekly P/NAV change was -1% and its 52-week range is 0.79x-1.19x.
RBC deck copper assumptions are $6.13/lb for 2026E and $6.00/lb for 2027E and 2028E, with a long-term price of $5.00/lb.

market_movers.rationale: Sector Perform with an $85 target based on a 50/50 blend of 1.50x NAV and 6.0x 2028E EBITDA. The multiples reflect challenges at Grasberg. Cost estimates were aligned with company guidance.

sector_views.rationale: Copper equities are pressured by AI-spending doubts and the Fed hold, while physical tightness and Chilean supply cuts support the structural supply case.

earnings_insights: FCX adjusted diluted EPS (RBC estimates): 2026E $3.54 vs prior $4.33, 2027E $4.80 vs prior $4.82, 2028E $5.45 vs prior $5.43.
FCX quarterly adjusted EPS 2026: Q1 $0.57 actual, Q2 $0.75 actual, Q3 $0.88 actual, Q4 $1.34 RBC estimate (prior estimate $2.01).
FCX adjusted EBITDA (RBC estimates): 2026E $12,738M vs prior $14,126M, 2027E $19,121M, 2028E $21,880M. Q4 2026E is $4,180M vs prior $5,699M.
RBC published company notes on FCX, FM, CIA and CS along with Q3 earnings quick takes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A steeper decline than the prior -2.6% estimate, which tightens copper supply.
A milder recovery than previously expected, which prolongs the supply deficit.
Signals tight physical copper availability in China.
Draws in Chinese stocks indicate strong physical demand or tight supply.

macro_indicators.reading: hold with two dissents in favour of a hike

risk_factors: Doubts over AI spending and a disconnect between AI capex and actual metals demand could weaken the copper demand narrative.
Grasberg operating disruptions and Indonesian political risk for FCX.
Near-term funding challenges, balance sheet de-leveraging, and significant balance sheet risk if copper falls sharply (FCX).
Chilean supply disruptions from lower ore grades and maintenance, and more frequent storms, strikes and seismic events at aging mines.
